target.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock
target.body:
## Summary

A long-running gateway can permanently deadlock its entire agent lane on a stuck OAuth auth-refresh. The runtime auth single-flight in `auth-controller.ts` stores the in-flight refresh promise in `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight`; every model turn that needs auth does `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` **with no timeout**. If the underlying provider auth hook (`prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` -> OAuth refresh, keychain read, or cross-agent file-lock wait) never settles, `refreshInFlight` is never cleared and **every subsequent turn hangs forever** awaiting it. The process stays alive and the port stays open, so it looks healthy while no replies are produced.

Observed in production: a gateway froze mid-day right after a token hit expiry. Process alive (11d uptime, port listening) but fully idle since the freeze, zero sockets to the provider, all threads parked, one never-resolving `await`. On-disk token was valid the whole time (a fresh process pre-warmed auth in ~0.7s), and no on-disk lock was held — i.e. a pure in-memory single-flight deadlock.

This adds a hard deadline so the single-flight promise **always** settles:

- New `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline()` + `RUNTIME_AUTH_REFRESH_HARD_TIMEOUT_MS` (300s) in `runtime-auth-refresh.ts`. 300s sits above the OAuth manager's own 120s call timeout plus a peer's 180s stale-lock window, so a legitimately slow cross-agent refresh still completes while a true hang is forced to reject.
- `refreshRuntimeAuth` wraps the refresh operation in that deadline; on timeout it rejects, the `.finally` clears `refreshInFlight`, and all waiters unblock with a descriptive error instead of hanging.
- The `.finally` clear is no longer gated on `generation`: a profile rotation during a slow/hung refresh must still release the handle it owns, otherwise a stale handle wedges the new generation. The existing `refreshInFlight === refreshPromise` identity guard still prevents clobbering a newer refresh.

No behavior change on the happy path (fast refresh resolves long before the deadline). The deadline is a backstop only.

## Repro / Test plan

- [x] `withRuntimeAuthRefreshDeadline` unit tests: rejects after the deadline when work never settles (fake timers), resolves/propagates when work wins the race, passes through unbounded for non-positive timeout, and the default exceeds the OAuth call + stale-lock budget.
- [x] `auth-controller` regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever sets `refreshInFlight`, then after advancing past the hard deadline the wedged handle rejects with `exceeded hard deadline` and is no longer the active in-flight handle.
- [x] Proof the test catches the bug: with the deadline neutralized (timeout `0` = unbounded), the regression test **times out / FAILS**; restored, it passes.
- [x] Current-head scoped run: see Evidence below.

Thanks @amittell.

---

## Update: complete the deadlock class (not just the refresh path)

A follow-up audit found the original commit only backstopped ONE of several entry paths into the same auth lock/gate machinery. Both remaining paths could still permanently wedge the agent lane the same way:

1. **Cold-start / profile-rotation path (critical).** `applyApiKeyInfo` (the path `initializeAuthProfile` and `advanceAuthProfile` use, and the first turn a watchdog restart lands on) awaited `resolveApiKeyForCandidate` and `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` — the exact hook that hung in production — with no deadline. A single shared local `withAuthDeadline` helper now wraps every auth boundary in `auth-controller.ts` (refresh AND cold-start), so a hung provider hook fails the turn over instead of deadlocking the lane.
2. **In-lock keychain / buildApiKey (high).** In `oauth-manager.ts`, `withRefreshCallTimeout` wrapped only the network refresh call; the in-lock keychain store load and `buildApiKey` ran un-deadlined while the cross-agent file lock was held, so a wedged keychain pinned the lock and chain-stalled every same-key refresher behind the un-timed `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh gate (`refreshQueue.enqueue` chains each caller on the previous tail with no timeout). The whole held-lock critical section is now bounded by `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` (150s), kept strictly between the 120s call timeout and the 180s stale window.

### Added proof
- `auth-controller` cold-start regression test: a `prepareProviderRuntimeAuth` that hangs forever on `initializeAuthProfile` now fails over within the deadline; **neutralizing the backstop makes the test time out / FAIL** (deadlock reproduced), confirming it catches the bug.
- `oauth-manager` invariant test pins `OAUTH_REFRESH_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS < OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS < stale`.
- All touched suites green at the current head; see Evidence below.

---

## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` still awaits `runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` in `auth-controller.ts` with no timeout, and the `.finally` clear is generation-gated, so one provider auth hook, keychain read, or cross-agent lock wait that never settles leaves the in-flight handle pending forever and every later model turn deadlocks awaiting it. The gateway process stays alive and its port stays open, so monitoring sees a healthy process while the agent lane produces no replies until a manual restart. This PR makes every runtime auth boundary settle: a hard 300s deadline on the single-flight refresh and cold-start paths, an ungated in-flight-handle clear, and a 150s bound on the whole held-lock OAuth critical section so a wedged keychain or hook cannot pin the cross-agent lock and chain-stall every same-key refresher queued behind it.

## Evidence

Rebased onto current `main` at 22376d80e163. The only conflict was `src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.ts`; it was resolved by keeping main's current `doRefreshOAuthTokenWithLock` body (the `KeyedAsyncQueue` refresh queue from #99691, the refresh-contention error classification from #101573, and `readBootstrapCredential({ store, ... })`) and re-applying only the `OAUTH_REFRESH_INLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` whole-section wrap on top.

Scoped test run at head ff8c5fea5a3700fcaff387ca66b7959ce148d8da:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts \
  src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
```

Sibling auth suites also pass at the same head: `oauth-refresh-queue`, `oauth-refresh-timeout`, `oauth-lock-timeout-classification`, `oauth-refresh-failure`, `oauth.concurrent-agents`, `oauth`, `oauth.fallback-to-main-agent`, `oauth.adopt-identity`, and `oauth.mirror-refresh` test files all green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ...` (2 Vitest shards passed). `tsgo` core lane exits 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on all seven changed files.

Production soak on a fork: gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06, and the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: gateway agent lane permanently deadlocks when one runtime auth refresh never settles; every later model turn hangs on an un-timed `await runtimeAuthState.refreshInFlight` while the process looks healthy.
Real environment tested: production gateways mac-mini.lan and rh-bot.lan have run this patch backported on a fork since 2026-06; the auth-refresh deadlock that previously froze the agent lane has not recurred.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/runtime-auth-refresh.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-controller.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth-manager.test.ts
Evidence after fix: 3 test files, 39 tests passed at head ff8c5fea5a3700fcaff387ca66b7959ce148d8da, including the hang-regression tests that time out and fail when the deadline backstop is neutralized; nine sibling oauth lock/queue/refresh test files also pass at the same head.
Observed result after fix: a hung provider auth hook or in-lock keychain wait now rejects at the deadline, the in-flight handle is cleared, waiting turns fail over with a descriptive error instead of deadlocking, and the production fork gateways have had no recurrence of the freeze.
What was not tested: live upstream-main gateway soak at this exact head; full build and broad CI lanes are left to PR CI.
